content:
VK2735: Viking Therapeutics' Dual GLP-1/GIP Peptide Enters Phase 3 — Research Dossier

Medical Disclaimer: Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Not FDA-approved for human use where applicable. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

What Is VK2735?

VK2735 is an investigational peptide dual agonist developed by Viking Therapeutics that simultaneously targets both the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) and the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR). This places it in the same mechanistic class as tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound by Eli Lilly), the most commercially successful obesity drug to date. VK2735 is in late-stage clinical development in two formulations: a once-weekly subcutaneous injectable (Phase 3) and a once-daily oral tablet (Phase 2 completed; Phase 3 planned).

Viking Therapeutics is a mid-cap clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on metabolic disease. VK2735 is its lead program and primary pipeline asset.

Mechanism of Action

VK2735 activates two distinct receptors with complementary roles in metabolic regulation:

  • GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R): Expressed in the hypothalamus, brainstem, pancreatic beta cells, stomach, and intestinal L-cells. GLP-1R agonism drives appetite suppression via central satiety circuits, slows gastric emptying (reducing caloric intake at meals), stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, and suppresses postprandial glucagon — the constellation of effects behind GLP-1-based weight loss.
  • GIP receptor (GIPR): Expressed in pancreatic beta cells, adipose tissue, and brain regions including the hypothalamus. GIP receptor agonism improves insulin sensitivity, modulates adipogenesis, and potentiates the GLP-1-driven insulin signal synergistically — which is why dual agonism consistently outperforms GLP-1R agonism alone in weight loss trials.

Viking has described VK2735 as having an optimized receptor binding profile for weight loss, though the specific receptor pharmacology (binding affinity ratios, receptor selectivity) has not been published in detail. The dual mechanism is well-validated by tirzepatide's SURMOUNT trial results, which showed 22.5% mean weight loss at 72 weeks — approximately 50% more than once-weekly semaglutide at a similar timepoint.

Key Research Findings

Phase 2 — Subcutaneous Injectable (VENTURE)

The Phase 2 VENTURE trial evaluated weekly subcutaneous VK2735 in adults with obesity. Key results (published in The Journal of Obesity):

  • Weight loss: Up to 14.7% mean placebo-adjusted body weight reduction after 13 weekly doses
  • No plateau: Weight loss curves had not plateaued at 13 weeks, suggesting continued efficacy with longer treatment
  • Tolerability: Predominantly mild to moderate GI adverse events (nausea, constipation); low discontinuation rate

Phase 2 — Oral Tablet (VENTURE-Oral, NCT06828055)

Completed in 2025. Full data presented at the European Congress on Obesity (ECO 2026, May 12, 2026):

  • Weight loss: Up to 12.2% mean weight loss from baseline at 13 weeks with the highest oral dose — statistically significant vs. placebo from Week 1 in all doses above 15 mg
  • Safety: 98% of drug-related adverse events were mild or moderate; discontinuation rates comparable to placebo
  • Competitive context: 12.2% at 13 weeks is among the highest reported for an oral GLP-1-class agent at this timepoint; oral semaglutide achieves 15–17% at the full 68-week treatment

Phase 3 — Subcutaneous Injectable (VANQUISH Program)

Two fully enrolled Phase 3 trials are ongoing:

  • VANQUISH-1: Pivotal 52-week trial in adults with obesity or overweight with weight-related comorbidity. Enrollment completed November 2025. Results expected 2027.
  • VANQUISH-2: 78-week trial in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes. Enrollment completed March 26, 2026. Results expected 2027.

Dosing in Research

Injectable: Once-weekly subcutaneous injection. Dose titration schedule used in VENTURE and VANQUISH trials (specific mg doses not fully disclosed publicly). Oral: Once-daily oral tablet; doses above 15 mg showed statistically significant weight loss in VENTURE-Oral; maximum dose tested in Phase 2 was not disclosed. Neither formulation is available outside clinical trials. This information is provided for educational purposes only.

Frequently Asked Questions

How does VK2735 compare to tirzepatide?

Both are dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist peptides. Tirzepatide is FDA-approved (Mounjaro for T2D 2022, Zepbound for obesity 2023) with up to 22.5% mean weight loss at 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-1. VK2735 is still investigational; no head-to-head trial exists. The 14.7% Phase 2 injectable result at 13 weeks is an encouraging early signal. VK2735's oral formulation is its key strategic differentiator — tirzepatide is currently injectable only.

What did the oral VK2735 Phase 2 trial show?

The VENTURE-Oral Phase 2 (NCT06828055) showed up to 12.2% mean weight loss from baseline at 13 weeks with the highest once-daily oral dose. This is a strong result for an oral obesity drug at 13 weeks. Adverse events were 98% mild or moderate. Viking completed an end-of-Phase 2 FDA meeting and plans to advance oral VK2735 into Phase 3 in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027.

What are the VANQUISH Phase 3 trials?

VANQUISH-1 (enrollment completed November 2025) is the pivotal 52-week injectable trial in adults with obesity/overweight with comorbidities. VANQUISH-2 (enrollment completed March 26, 2026) is a 78-week trial in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes. Both are double-blind and placebo-controlled. Results are expected in 2027; positive results would support an FDA NDA submission for the injectable formulation.

Research Limitations

  • No Phase 3 results published as of November 2026; VANQUISH studies expected to complete in 2027.
  • No head-to-head comparison with tirzepatide or semaglutide in human trials.
  • Specific peptide sequence and receptor pharmacology data not publicly disclosed.
  • Oral Phase 3 not yet started as of this dossier; oral approval requires a separate registration program.
  • Long-term cardiovascular outcomes, pancreatitis risk, and rare adverse event profile not established.

Disclaimer

VK2735 is an investigational compound not approved by the FDA or any regulatory authority worldwide for any indication as of November 2026. This dossier is intended for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice. Do not attempt to obtain or use this compound outside of an authorized clinical trial. Consult a licensed healthcare provider for any weight management or metabolic health concerns.
